title: Derived internal Hom commutes naturally with slice restriction, compatibly with successive restrictions.
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with Grothendieck topology $J$, and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Use the unbounded derived categories $D(R)$ and $D(R_U)$ of module sheaves, in one chosen localization morphism universe, and suppose these derived categories exist for every $U\in\mathcal C$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $R_U=R|_U$ for the ring on the slice site $\mathcal C/U$, and for $f:V\to U$ use restriction along $(W\to V)\mapsto(W\to V\to U)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $r_U:D(R)\to D(R_U)$ and $r_f:D(R_U)\to D(R_V)$ be the induced termwise derived restrictions [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. Let $c_f:r_f r_U\xrightarrow{\sim}r_V$ be the canonical comparison, induced by the sectionwise identity on module restrictions and the composition comparison for induced derived functors. Put $H=R\mathcal Hom_R$ and $H_U=R\mathcal Hom_{R_U}$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

There exist natural isomorphisms, in both derived inputs,
$$e_U(L,M):r_UH(L,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_U(r_UL,r_UM)$$
for every $U$, and
$$s_f(A,B):r_fH_U(A,B)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_V(r_fA,r_fB)$$
for every $f:V\to U$ and $A,B\in D(R_U)$, such that for all $L,M\in D(R)$
$$H_V(c_{f,L}^{-1},c_{f,M})\circ s_f(r_UL,r_UM)\circ r_f(e_U(L,M))
=e_V(L,M)\circ c_{f,H(L,M)}.$$
Here $H_V$ is contravariant in its first input, so $c_{f,L}^{-1}:r_VL\to r_fr_UL$ is the first argument of its displayed morphism. No boundedness, flatness, or finite-generation hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Use the coherent ordinary Hom-complex comparisons a_U and b_f from [lem-ringed-hom-restriction-ordinary]. Slice restriction preserves K-injectives by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], and relocalization preserves them by [lem-sp-site-relocalization-kinjective-independent-ring]. The normalized descent theorem [lem-ringed-hom-restriction-comparison-descent] therefore produces derived comparisons e_U and s_f on all inputs of the respective derived categories.

The transported composite of e_U and s_f is normalized against the transported composite of a_U and b_f by [lem-ringed-hom-restriction-composition-normalization]. Ordinary coherence identifies the latter with a_V. Uniqueness of normalized descent [lem-ringed-hom-restriction-comparison-descent] identifies the derived composite with e_V. The componentwise compatibility equivalence in that node is exactly the required equation, with the prescribed inverse in the contravariant argument.
